findings.baseline: A1 OFF on source 2854fa4 reproduced control_end 126.26 and fine 28.40 SIM s exactly (third identical OFF run).
b1: Forward stage passed (53 movement slices vs 57 OFF) but schedule handed over at .0608 after a .11 command and the error still fell .0608 -> .0331 -> .007 -> -.0066 under .012/.01 model commands: carry-over lasts several slices, beyond the one-slice fit.
Likely mechanism (hypothesis): a small nonzero command uses the moving damping rather than the stop damping, so the chassis coasts; the one-lag fit was dominated by small-command data.
Recovering from the overshoot at the .01 floor removed most of the saving; stage-4 yaw RGB for slot r3 was then outside learned support at SIM 40.65.
findings.claims: Schedule v2 (bundle v32) is not qualified; no speed or success claim.

assessment.ceiling: Even a perfect fine-stage schedule can save at most part of 28.4 SIM s of a 126.3 SIM s synchronous mission (~5-15%), and each faster approach risks leaving pose-model support.
assessment.larger_opportunity: Fine alignment takes 28.4 SIM s synchronously but 51-78 SIM s in realtime runs; the realtime gap (decision latency and idle leases) is larger than any gain-schedule saving and overlaps Codex rolling work (#131).
